title: DevX scratchpad — gap hunt + quick fixes
content:
Morning quick log (10 Mar) — brain dump for doc gaps, sample apps, tutorial fixes. 

Top-of-mind priorities:
- Fix inconsistencies in JS SDK quickstart: auth header example vs SDK helper (users copy pasted curl that uses `api_key` param) — high friction for new users.
- Add a tiny sample app that shows streaming chat + function-calls + structured JSON output (1 page + runnable repo).
- Document error modes & retries for streaming endpoints (what to expect on partial stream failures).
- Short checklist for tutorials: ensure every tutorial ends with expected output snippet and exact curl/py/js commands that work today.

Backlog items (quick estimates):
- JS quickstart auth alignment (30–60m): update code block, add one-liner to explain API key scoping.
- Streaming error doc (1.5–2h): create a small section in hosted-api docs + sample response traces.
- Sample app: streaming-chat-to-slack (3–4d): prototype + README + one test harness.
- Tutorial smoke tests (2d): make a tiny CI job that runs example snippets and compares outputs (or at least checks exit codes).

Notes to self / unfinished thoughts:
- On function-calling example: current tutorial shows a single function. Add an example with two functions and a resolver that picks based on user intent. Show the JSON schema for each function AND an example of how the SDK maps results to typed objects.
- Consider `redwood devx init` generator to scaffold sample apps (just a thought; low priority).
- We should surface latency/cost tradeoffs in docs for streaming vs non-streaming calls (even 1 paragraph).

Concrete doc edits to ship this week (actionable):
1) Update docs/quickstart/js.md: replace `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` vs `x-api-key` confusion; include minimal JS fetch + SDK client snippet. (assigned to Marco)
2) Create docs/streams/errors.md: short troubleshooting + sample partial stream payloads + recommended retry window. (I'll draft)
3) Create sample repo skeleton: devx-samples/streaming-chat-to-slack with README + env var notes + deploy instructions (Talia will prototype).

Scratch commands / snippets to include in the small samples (pasteable):
- Minimal fetch example (JS):
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'hello'}] })
  });
- Stream client note: show how to handle SSE chunks and detect truncated JSON; recommend `max_retry` backoff 300–1000ms.

Questions / blockers:
- Who owns the canonical SDK copy for examples? We have duplication across repos (devx-sdk, examples, docs). Need a short sync with platform docs owner to align.
- Is there an accepted pattern for exposing API key rotation in sample apps? We should add a short appendix with KMS/HSM note for private deployments.

Micro UX ideas (parking lot):
- Add a little "Try this in your browser" widget to the quickstart that runs against a sandbox key and shows streaming output in a small console box. (nice but depends on sandbox infra)
- Inline cost estimate microcard for each sample: estimated tokens per run + typical runtime on dedicated pools.

End-of-day checklist (what I want done before I close this doc):
- [ ] Draft streams/errors.md initial section
- [ ] Leave inline comments on PR #412 about auth snippet
- [ ] Create skeleton repo with README and issue template
- [ ] Quick Slack ping to @platform-docs to propose single-source-of-truth for examples

Random notes and fragments to capture: 
- Example error trace for partial stream: `{"type":"delta","content":"...","partial":true}
  then final: {"type":"done","status":200}` — add this example to troubleshooting.
- Keep function names short in samples: `getWeather`, `lookupUser` not `GetDetailedWeatherForGpsCoordinates`.
- TODO: add a tiny test that asserts the sample README command exits 0.

If I get time today: sketch the streaming-chat-to-slack README sections and a simple diagram (sequence: user -> client -> Redwood API -> function resolver -> external API -> function result -> client).

---
Last quick mental note: aim for copy that reduces cognitive load — 1 command per step, explicit env var names, clear expected outputs. If it's ambiguous, we lost the user.
